answer: An applicant needs two opal seals from curators, and each curator locks 60 credits in an oasis pool per seal. A fake sealed identity burns both seals: 120 credits per fake, so 1,000 fakes put 120,000 credits at risk. An honest applicant pays only 5 credits per seal, 10 in total; curators lose nothing. Applications arrive tide by tide; a seal counts only if its curator's oasis deposit has a distinct funding source. A curator collusion ring fails: its seals sit in the pool, any challenger may present fraud proof to burn them, and seals sharing one deposit never count twice.
